paragraphs.text: Wellington R1037 of 12 Operational Training Unit took off from Chipping Warden on a night training flight on 20 October 1941. It crashed in Chipping Warden village at about 23:10 while attempting to go round again, and caught fire. Pilot Officer Kenneth Farnes was killed. Pilot Officer Cecil Harry Hayes was seriously injured and died of his injuries on 21 October. Farnes was 30 and is buried at Brookwood Military Cemetery; Hayes is buried in Malden churchyard.
A plaque to Kenneth Farnes is fixed to the side of a private house in Hogg Lane, Chipping Warden. War Memorials Online records no inscription, builder, dedication date or custodian for it.

notes: Only two airmen are named in any source read: Farnes and Hayes. Our record says 3 survived and lists Brumby, Newton, Jenner, Brathwaite, Crompton; no source I read supports either, so the narrative should drop them. Source lists no survivors; IBCC and WMO both say 2 died. IBCC's own Farnes page (loss/107393) returned HTTP 429 three times, so its detail is unread; the IBCC Farnes link is taken from the Hayes crew list. IBCC record for Hayes gives 21 Oct against CWGC Farnes 20 Oct for the crash; the crash was about 23:10 on the 20th and Hayes died 5am next day, so the dates reconcile. Roles: WMO names Farnes as pilot; IBCC names Hayes pilot; likely instructor/pupil but no source says, so unresolved. Wikipedia's IBCC/CWGC citations mean it is not independent. The record's existing maintainer (Chipping Warden and Edgcote Parish Council) is unsupported: the plaque is on a private house and no source names a custodian. No IWM War Memorials Register entry for this plaque found by search; the IWM entries for Chipping Warden cover the church WWI board and a WWII brass plaque with 3 names. Search snippets (not fetchable, page returned 404) from a Royal British Legion Byfield District branch page say the plaque is in Hogg End and the aircraft clipped a cottage roof; unverified lead, not used. Lead: Geograph photo search for Farnes/Hogg End found nothing. Site coordinates in our record (52.136,-1.272) differ slightly from WMO (52.134087,-1.27351). The 'RAF Info Chorley OTU/079' reference in our record was not checked. The two remembrance events in our record (P/O Barnett, OTU/013) are unrelated to this memorial and should be removed.
